newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia stocks dive in thin trade, no changes seen.
newsitem.headline: Croatia stocks dive in thin trade, no changes seen.

text.p: Croatian stocks took a dive to close mostly lower on Thursday in dwindling trade and analysts predicted the trend would continue for some time, with large investors holding back.

"I expect the situation to be more or less the same in the near future," said an analyst of the I.F.C. brokerage, adding investors were still scared by a recent government announcement to annul some 9,000 employee buyout contracts.
He said the prices of stocks, with the exception of fully listed drug firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka, both of which are sold abroad, were too high and "could go a bit further down".
Of nine active issues on Thursday eight fell and one was flat. Volume shrank to 4,488 shares and so did turnover, totalling a slim 2.5 million kuna ($469,000).
"You can tell that there are no big investors. Whatever trading is made is either sounding of the market or small individual purchases," the analyst said.
The day's biggest decliner was electric cables maker Elka, which shed 55 kuna from last weeek to end at 215 kuna, selling 524 shares.
Bluechips Pliva and Zagreback Banka went down, in line with their downward trend in London.
Pliva lost 50 kuna to close at 13,450 on volume of only 21 shares.
Zagrebacka fell 20 kuna to 1,000. It was Thursday's most active issue with 1,324 units traded.
Hotelier Jadranturist was the only stock to hold its ground at 290 kuna on a volume of 631 shares.
Hoteliers Laguna Porec and Suncani Hvar went down. Laguna lost 5 kuna to close at 1,145 on volume of 161 shares and Suncani shed 1 kuna, closing at 60 kuna, with 441 shares sold.
Among the decliners were also confectioner Kras, down 10 kuna to 510 on volume of 136 shares, and food processor Podravka, which fell 5 kuna to 220, trading 1,200 shares. ($ = 5.321 Croatian Kuna)
